content: Following a 2014 separation, spouses sought the division of three properties in Gela, with the wife claiming credits for parental inheritance and child maintenance. Under Art. 192 CC, the right to reimbursement for personal funds used for common assets requires rigorous proof of the funds' personal nature and their specific reinvestment, failing which the 50/50 split remains. Regarding liabilities, child maintenance is an unpawnable and non-compensable credit due to its alimentary nature, thus it cannot be set off against division debts. Finally, if a family home is assigned to the same spouse who becomes its exclusive owner through division, the right of habitation is extinguished by confusion; consequently, the property must be valued at its full market price without any depreciation when calculating the settlement due to the other spouse.
